clue.text: Cats brightened up by cat's-meat after a measure?

indicators.note: after says the meat comes behind the measure in the answer

parts.note: a foot is a unit of length, twelve inches
lights are animal lungs, traditionally sold as cheap meat for cats

explanation.surface: A cat, fed on offal after its portion is measured out, seems cheered up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats here is the stage musical, lit from the front edge of the stage; the surface wants pet cats cheered by their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The row of lamps along the front of a stage illuminates a show such as the musical Cats.

clue.text: Device for triangulating spheres .

parts.note: the wooden triangle used to rack up the balls in snooker or pool, rather than a surveying instrument

explanation.surface: A surveying instrument for measuring globes.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker balls are packed into a triangle at the start, and that rack shares its name with a structure holding something in shape.

clue.text: Manipulator shot a poet to pieces

indicators.note: a poet shot to pieces is broken up, so the letters of shot a poet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manipulator gunned down a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who treats the body by manipulating bones and joints.

clue.text: Beastly pair of army supporters?

parts.note: two animals holding up the royal coat of arms, read as arm-y supporters rather than fans of the army

explanation.surface: Two nasty fans of the military.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the supporters are figures either side of a shield; the British royal arms have two beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The two heraldic beasts flanking the British royal coat of arms are its supporters.

clue.text: Figure N formation we hear during bombardment

indicators.note: a formation is a rearrangement, so the letters of figure and N are reordered

explanation.surface: A figure seen in a formation we spot during an air raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of shooting artillery is what is heard in a bombardment.

clue.text: Gold found in river — one in spate

indicators.note: found in puts the gold inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold is panned from a flooded river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing flood of water is a river in spate.

clue.text: May be "organic", eg the colon?

parts.note: one sense is a register knob on a church organ; the other is a punctuation mark, as the colon is, the bowel only on the surface

explanation.surface: A question of whether the colon counts as an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Organ registers and punctuation marks both share this name, so a colon is one kind.

clue.text: Passage in which solo is not to be played

definitions.text: Passage in which solo is not to be played

parts.words: Passage in which solo is not to be played
parts.note: a musical direction for all performers to play together, so no soloist stands alone

explanation.surface: A section of music where nobody plays alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction meaning 'all' marks a passage for the whole ensemble.

clue.text: Place of rest for 11 with broken cane, maybe

parts.note: a rooster (11 across) rests on a perch

indicators.note: broken means the letters of cane are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird's resting place with a broken cane, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer to 11 across, the cock.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for perhaps or possibly.

clue.text: Excelling in virtue my singer in the wilderness? How smug!

definitions.text: Excelling in virtue my singer in the wilderness?
definitions.meaning: more saintly than 'thou beside me singing in the wilderness' from FitzGerald's Omar Khayyam

explanation.surface: A self-righteous remark about the singer of Omar Khayyam's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'thou' is the companion 'beside me singing in the Wilderness' in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more saintly than the person addressed, and self-righteously smug, are both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Instrument taking wind notwithstanding (in short) the Navy

parts.note: notwithstanding means although, shortened to its informal form altho
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A wind instrument played regardless, perhaps by a naval band.
explanation.walkthrough: '(in short)' signals the clipped spelling ALTHO of although.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brass instrument of the saxhorn family, played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Cock house member

definitions.meaning: one who perches in a hen house, its roost

explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is the male fowl, and it is also one that settles on a perch in the hen house.

clue.text: Recalling with some point the case of O

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
addressing someone with 'O', as in 'O Lord', uses the grammatical case of address, the vocative

explanation.surface: A remark about remembering a sharp argument over a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The vocative is the Latin grammatical case for addressing someone, as in 'O Caesar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings memories to mind is said to call them up, which is what recalling describes.

clue.text: Race hard after starting flag

indicators.note: the hard letter comes after the flag, which takes the starting place

parts.note: the flag or yellow flag is a type of iris plant
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough race begins once the starter's flag drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like the starter's flag but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A people or nation can be called a race, here the people of Ireland.

clue.text: Trade mark maintained within broad limits

indicators.note: within puts the piece for maintained inside those letters
the limits of a word are its first and last letters, here of broad

parts.note: to run a business is to maintain it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: A trademark kept up within wide boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A product's distinctive name or logo is a trade mark, also called its make.

clue.text: Last of army left southern cliff, giving access to invader

indicators.note: left means the letter departs from the cliff's name

parts.note: Beachy Head is a chalk headland on the south coast of England

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of army

explanation.surface: The army's rearguard left a southern cliff top, letting the enemy in.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothold seized on an enemy shore lets an invading force come ashore.

clue.text: Board train without right and maybe get laughed at

parts.note: to board a train is to get on or enter it

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the word train

explanation.surface: A passenger boards a train without a seat reserved and gets mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: one who amuses an audience may well be laughed at.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse an audience as a comedian does is to invite their laughter.

clue.text: Long-term remittance man

parts.note: one paid a yearly sum for life, rather than the colonial exile paid to stay abroad

explanation.surface: An exile living for years on money sent from home.
explanation.walkthrough: A remittance man was a black sheep paid by his family to stay in the colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receiving a fixed yearly income for life is regularly sent payments over a long term.

clue.text: London club, but not part of the Temple

definitions.text: London club, but not part of the Temple

parts.words: London club, but not part of the Temple
parts.note: a gentlemen's club in Pall Mall named after a temple of the goddess Athena, though nothing to do with the Inns of Court called the Temple

explanation.surface: A London club is said to sit outside the legal precinct of the Temple.
explanation.walkthrough: The Temple is the London area holding two of the Inns of Court for barristers; the club's name means a temple of Athena.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a famous gentlemen's club in Pall Mall, taken from a Greek temple of the goddess Athena.

clue.text: Suet well cooked a winner when served by him

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so the letters of suet are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is a tennis serve that wins the point outright

explanation.surface: A suet pudding served by a man is a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him', the man who serves the ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, the person referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Disfigured one intruder, and became united

indicators.note: intruder says the one forces its way inside the word for disfigured

parts.note: disfigured means spoiled or marred
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scarred intruder who then got wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be joined as husband and wife is to become united in wedlock.

clue.text: Turning point in an open-and-shut case

definitions.text: Turning point in an open-and-shut case

parts.words: Turning point in an open-and-shut case
parts.note: a pivot on which a lid or door swings, as in a box that opens and shuts; the surface suggests a decisive moment in a simple legal case

explanation.surface: A decisive moment in a legal case that seemed obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivoting joint lets a lid or door swing, so it is literally the point a case turns on.

clue.text: Serious disorder arising from prawns with avocado

indicators.note: the answer arises from letters running across the words with avocado

explanation.surface: Food poisoning blamed on a prawn and avocado starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread chaos and destruction is the sense of the word, as in 'wreak' it.

clue.text: Flat for Virginia, devout daughter

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
pi is informal for pious, devout

explanation.surface: An apartment for a pious daughter named Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking liveliness, as a flat remark is insipid.

clue.text: Not safe when 90, nor must it be tampered with

indicators.note: tampered with means interfered with, so the letters of nor must it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about something unsafe at ninety that must not be meddled with.
explanation.walkthrough: The 90 is the radioactive isotope strontium-90, a fallout hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: The isotope with mass number 90 of this element is a dangerous radioactive product of nuclear fallout.

clue.text: Maybe ground under repair if it's being treated

definitions.text: Maybe ground under repair if it's being treated

parts.words: Maybe ground under repair if it's being treated
parts.note: a back tooth that grinds food, under repair when the dentist treats it; the surface suggests a sports ground under maintenance

explanation.surface: A playing field closed for repairs while it is treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding back tooth is one that may be ground down and gets filled by a dentist.

clue.text: Big markets — Portia loses her shirt on 'em

indicators.note: on says the trimmed name is placed after the short word

parts.note: 'em is a short form of them, taken as its letters

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the name Portia

parts.note: a T-shirt, so her shirt is the letter T

explanation.surface: Portia, the Shakespeare heroine, gambles her shirt on a bet in the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: To lose one's shirt is to lose everything gambling; here Portia loses only her T.
explanation.definitionFit: Large commercial centres or trading places are called by this plural of a Latin word for market.

clue.text: One expelled by Bible Society

parts.note: in Genesis Abraham's son by Hagar is cast out into the desert, a man thrust out by the society of the Bible

explanation.surface: A member thrown out of a Bible study group.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham's elder son and his mother Hagar are driven out into the wilderness.

clue.text: Inactive queen?

parts.note: a queen of Carthage in Virgil, whose name splits as did and zero, as if she did nothing

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary queen of Carthage whose name reads as 'did nothing'.

clue.text: Native stalker camouflaged under heath

indicators.note: camouflaged means disguised, so the letters of under heath are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribesman stalking prey hidden in the heathland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman who hunts enemies and keeps their skulls as trophies.
